chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yahya ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who said to me, 'Buy this cloth and this animal for me, specifying it, and I will profit you in it with such and such.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with that.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Let him buy it, and you should not obligate the sale before he obligates it or you buy it.'

key_terms.أُرْبِحَكَ: I will profit you (promise of extra gain)
key_terms.يَسْتَوْجِبَهَا: he obligates it (binds himself to the purchase)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a valid profit-sharing purchase agreement in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the permissibility of 'buying on credit with profit' (bay' al-mu'ajjal bi-ziyadah) by distinguishing it from a binding contract until the agent actually acquires the item. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) permits the arrangement where one asks another to purchase a specific good with a promised extra profit, provided the agent is not obligated to the sale until the purchase is complete, thereby avoiding the uncertainty (gharar) of pre-binding a sale. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on ensuring the subject matter exists and is owned before the profit-sharing agreement becomes legally enforceable.
